text: [cheerful, proud] Canada. Free healthcare. Maple syrup. Moose crossing the road like they pay rent.

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, slow, dead serious] I do not pay rent. I collect it.
[startled] Okay, that moose is terrifying.
[excited, to camera] But here’s the thing. Canada also gives you three money cheat codes. And most people never press the buttons.
[hyped] Use them right, and a regular person could retire a millionaire. Seriously.
[friendly] Welcome to Finnomics! I’m Finn, I’m fourteen, and yes, this toque is new. My piggy bank is still a moth hotel.
[quick aside] Not financial advice. I’m fourteen. And very cold.
[explaining] So, the three cheat codes. The T F S A. The R R S P. And the F H S A.
[playful] They sound like Wi-Fi passwords. But they are basically shields that block the Tax Moose.

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, offended] I heard that.
[explaining] Cheat code number one. The Tax-Free Savings Account. Grandma explains it best.
[sweet, southern] Every fish you catch through this hole, you keep. All of it. No moose gets a bite.
[explaining] Money you put in a TFSA can grow, and when you take it out, you pay zero tax on the growth. Zero!
[explaining] For 2026, you can add seven thousand dollars. And unused room piles up. If you’ve been an adult since 2009 and never used it, you could have a hundred and nine thousand dollars of room!

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, frustrated] Why is there a force field around this hole?
[proud] Because it’s a TFSA, honey. Shoo.
[explaining] And if you take money out, you get that room back next year. It’s flexible. Like a hockey player. Or Grandma.
[proud] So I opened a TFSA! And I put my money in it! And it earned... half a percent.
[gentle, teasing] Sugar, you bought a race car and left it in the garage.
[realising] The biggest TFSA mistake. It’s not a savings account. It’s a basket. You choose what goes inside.
[explaining] Cash, sure. But many long-term investors fill it with low-cost index funds. Tiny pieces of hundreds of companies, all in one bucket.
[hyped] Now the race car is actually racing!
[wise] And don’t put all your eggs in one basket, sugar. Unless the basket holds a thousand companies.
[explaining] That’s the magic. One index fund can own pieces of thousands of companies. If one company flops, you barely notice.
[playful] It’s like a poutine. If one fry is soggy, the poutine still slaps.
[serious] Two TFSA traps. Trap one: putting in too much. The CRA charges one percent per month on the extra.

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, delighted] One percent. Every. Month.
[explaining] Your room shows in your CRA account, but it can lag behind. So keep your own records too.
[explaining] Trap two: treating your TFSA like a casino. If you day-trade a lot inside it, the CRA can decide it’s a business, and tax it.
[calm] Slow and steady, sugar. Like curling.
[confused] Grandma, curling is literally sweeping ice really fast.
[dry] Hush.
[explaining] Before we invest a single loonie, we need a snow shovel. An emergency fund.
[calm] Life always sends a snowstorm, sugar. The car breaks. The furnace quits. The dog eats a mitten.
[explaining] Without savings, that surprise goes on a credit card at around twenty percent interest. Ouch.
[explaining] A common goal is three to six months of your basic expenses, kept somewhere safe and easy to reach. Start small. Even five hundred dollars helps.
[proud] Mine’s in a high-interest savings account. And a little in a coffee can. Old habits.
[sporty announcer] Cheat code number two! The Registered Retirement Savings Plan!
[explaining] Here’s the trick. Money you put in lowers your taxable income today. So the government can send you a refund.
[explaining] Put in a thousand dollars, and depending on your tax bracket, you might get a few hundred back. Like scoring a goal and getting the puck returned with a bonus.

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, patient, menacing] Enjoy it. I will be waiting at retirement.
[explaining] He’s right. RRSP money gets taxed when you take it out. The hope is you’re in a lower tax bracket when you’re retired.
[explaining] Your room is eighteen percent of last year’s income, up to thirty-three thousand eight hundred and ten dollars for 2026.
[excited] And if your job matches your RRSP contributions? That’s free money. That’s an assist. Never skip an assist!
[explaining] Cheat code number three is for future home buyers. The First Home Savings Account.
[explaining] It’s like the TFSA and the RRSP had a baby. Money going in can lower your taxes, and money coming out for your first home is tax-free.

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, horrified] Tax-free on the way in AND the way out? That is illegal.
[smug] It’s literally the law, buddy.
[explaining] You can add eight thousand dollars a year, up to forty thousand total. If you might buy a home one day, look into it early.
[deflated] Forty thousand won’t buy a house in Toronto. But it might buy the front door.
[curious] But how does a normal person get to a million? I asked the hardest-working guy in Canada.
[cheerful, fast] One stick a day, bud. Every day. That’s how you build a dam!
[explaining] That’s compounding. Your money earns money, then that money earns money too. Boring at first, then huge.
[explaining] Say you invest seven thousand a year in your TFSA from age twenty-five to sixty-five, and it grows seven percent a year. You’d put in two hundred eighty thousand.
[amazed] And end up with about one point four million dollars. Tax-free!
[serious] Start ten years later, at thirty-five? About six hundred sixty thousand. Less than half!
[wise, chill] Ya can’t build a dam in the last week of summer, eh.
[quick] Seven percent isn’t guaranteed, by the way. Some years go up, some go down. But time is your best friend.
[encouraging] Can’t do seven thousand a year? Nobody starts there. Even a hundred dollars a month for forty years, at seven percent, could grow to around two hundred sixty thousand.
[cheerful] Small sticks still make a dam, bud!
[explaining] Now, the sneaky leak. Fees.
[explaining] Some investment funds charge around two percent a year. Low-cost index funds can charge a quarter of a percent or less.
[explaining] Two percent sounds tiny. But on a hundred thousand dollars over thirty years, it could cost you more than two hundred and fifty thousand dollars!
[shocked] That’s a lot of syrup, bud!
[firm] Always check the fee. It’s called the M E R. Lower is usually better.
[smooth, sneaky] Psst. Why invest when you could buy a snowmobile on credit?
[annoyed] Mister Swipe! What are you doing in Canada?
[proud] Card interest here is around twenty percent. I LOVE it here.
[explaining] And that’s the point. If your card charges twenty percent and your investments might earn seven, pay off the card first. That’s a guaranteed win.
[shivering, chattering] I’m f-f-freezing. I’m going back to the mall.
[explaining] Here’s the laziest trick that works. Automate it.
[explaining] Set an automatic transfer for payday. The money moves into your TFSA before you even see it.
[playful] It’s called paying yourself first. You can’t spend money that already left the building.
[distant, outraged] Hey! I was going to spend that!
[explaining] Then every time you get a raise, bump the transfer up a little. Future you will send a thank-you card.
[cheerful] Robots building dams? I love it, eh!
[coach voice] Okay team, here’s the game plan. A common order lots of people use.
[counting] One. Build a small emergency fund, so surprises don’t go on a credit card.
[counting] Two. Pay off high-interest debt.
[counting] Three. Grab any employer match. Never skip an assist.
[counting] Four. Fill your TFSA, and your FHSA if you want a first home.
[counting] Five. Use your RRSP, especially as your income grows.
[counting] Six. Pick low-fee investments, automate it, and let time do the work.
[cheering] And never feed the moose more than you have to!
[warm, sincere] Getting rich in Canada isn’t about one big win. It’s one stick a day. Use the cheat codes, keep fees low, and start early.

voice: Joe - Deep Voice Evil Villain Final Boss
text: [deep, sad] So I get nothing?
[kind] You still get some. Just less. Now go eat a pine cone.
[upbeat] If this helped, subscribe to Finnomics. It’s free. Even the moose subscribed.
[whispering, teasing] Next time: inflation. Why a candy bar costs way more than it did for Grandma.
[offscreen, proud] Thirty-five cents, sugar!
